steps.label: ORPHANED ROW
steps.sub: the thing it points to doesn't exist

code:
SELECT o.OrderId, o.CustomerId
FROM dbo.Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN dbo.Customers AS c
    ON o.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
WHERE c.CustomerId IS NULL
  AND o.CustomerId IS NOT NULL;
caption: Start from every order, try to find its customer, keep the ones that came back empty.
The same Execute step as every check — nothing changes for a referential integrity check.

code:
SELECT 'Orders -> Customers' AS Relationship,
       CAST(o.OrderId AS VARCHAR(20)) AS OrphanedKey
FROM dbo.Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN dbo.Customers AS c
    ON o.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
WHERE c.CustomerId IS NULL AND o.CustomerId IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT 'OrderLines -> Orders',
       CAST(ol.OrderLineId AS VARCHAR(20))
FROM dbo.OrderLines AS ol
LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders AS o ON ol.OrderId = o.OrderId
WHERE o.OrderId IS NULL;
caption: One run, every orphaned row across every relationship you care about.
A real SSMS results grid — orphan rows read exactly like any other check's output.
